trajectory.patch:
The assertion failure `(var_cnt == sizeof(test_data) is false)` in `tests/subsys/fs/fcb/src/fcb_test_append.c` indicates that the `fcb_walk` function is not finding all the entries that were previously appended. This specific failure occurs in the `test_fcb_append_crc_disabled` test, which uses an FCB instance with `FCB_FLAGS_CRC_DISABLED` set.

The `test_fcb_append` function appends 128 entries with lengths from 0 to 127. The `fcb_test_data_walk_cb` callback function, used by `fcb_walk`, expects the `k`-th entry (0-indexed) to have a length of `k`. It also uses `var_cnt` as a running counter, incrementing it after each successful entry validation. If all 128 entries are found in order, `var_cnt` should be 128 at the end of `fcb_walk`. The failure implies `var_cnt` is less than 128.

The key difference between the passing `test_fcb_append_2sectors` (CRC enabled) and the failing `test_fcb_append_crc_disabled` (CRC disabled) points to an issue in the FCB core logic related to handling entries when CRC is disabled.

In the FCB, an entry typically consists of a header, length field, data, an optional CRC field, and an end marker. When CRC is disabled, the `crc_sz` variable (representing the size of the CRC field) should be 0, otherwise it's `FCB_CRC_SZ` (typically 4 bytes). Both `fcb_append` and `fcb_getnext` (used by `fcb_walk`) must correctly account for this `crc_sz` when calculating offsets and sizes.

A common bug pattern in such scenarios is that the read logic (in `fcb_getnext_in_sector`) might incorrectly use the compile-time constant `FCB_CRC_SZ` (4 bytes) when calculating the offset to the end marker, even when the entry was written with `crc_sz = 0` (CRC disabled). If an entry was written without a CRC (end marker immediately after data), but the read function expects a 4-byte CRC field, it would look for the end marker 4 bytes too late, leading to misinterpretation of flash data and premature termination of the `fcb_walk`.

The fix involves ensuring that `fcb_getnext_in_sector` uses the dynamically determined `crc_sz` variable (which is 0 when CRC is disabled) when calculating the offset to read the end marker, instead of the constant `FCB_CRC_SZ`.

Assuming `subsys/fs/fcb/fcb_getnext.c` contains the `fcb_getnext_in_sector` function and a line similar to the one below for reading the end marker:

subsys/fs/fcb/fcb_getnext.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
	rc = flash_area_read(fap, entry_loc.fe_data_off + entry_loc.fe_data_len + FCB_CRC_SZ,
			     &end_magic, sizeof(end_magic));
========
	rc = flash_area_read(fap, entry_loc.fe_data_off + entry_loc.fe_data_len + crc_sz,
			     &end_magic, sizeof(end_magic));
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
